uncited: The RGB Network Layer is the final stage of the neural volume rendering pipeline responsible for predicting the RGB color value at a given 3D position.
It builds on [MLP with Positional Encoding](2416-mlp-with-positional-encoding.md) by processing positional embeddings and view direction encodings to produce a color vector.
**Preload Weights:** Load the RGB network weights into shared memory.
Compute second hidden layer `hid2` using ReLU on `hid1`.
Compute output buffer `hid1` (reused) using ReLU on `hid2`.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of samples and network depth.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Depends on the number of hidden units and layers.
*   **When to Use:** Standard neural volume rendering pipelines requiring RGB color prediction.
*   **When Not to Use:** When density prediction (use Sigma Network Layer) or post-processing refinement (use CNN Post-Processing Network) is required.
The RGB Network Layer is part of the neural volume rendering pipeline, specifically within the context of neural implicit representations like NeRF and its variants.
